paper_title: Poor Man's Agentic Modeling: Simulating Large LLM-Agent Societies on a Laptop

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Simulating societies of many large language model (LLM) agents is expensive, yet the questions asked of such simulations are usually macroscopic: phase behaviour, stylised facts, and scaling with the number of agents $N$, not the cognition of any single agent. We turn a statistical-physics observation into a method: replace each LLM agent by a low-parameter model fitted from a few hundred to a few thousand cheap queries, then run the society at any $N$ on a laptop. Whether this works is decided before the simulation runs, chiefly by what each agent perceives. We introduce an [interaction order x memory] taxonomy that maps perception and memory to an effective theory and a predicted $N$-trend of the surrogate error. We validate it on a faithful reimplementation of the LLM macroeconomy EconAgent and seven further named LLM simulations, with agent decisions cloned from genuine LLM elicitations (primarily DeepSeek) for a few dollars; the predicted error trends hold cell by cell, and the two refuted predictions, both on a strongly saturating response and traced to its curvature, are themselves matched quantitatively by the theory with no free parameters.

We validate it on faithful reimplementation of the LLM macroeconomy EconAgent and seven further named LLM simulations, with agent decisions cloned from genuine LLM elicitations (primarily DeepSeek) for few dollars; the predicted error trends hold cell by cell, and the two refuted predictions, both on strongly saturating response and traced to its curvature, are themselves matched quantitatively by the theory with no free parameters. sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: A growing body of work builds simulations in which each agent is large language model: generative towns, LLM macroeconomies, social-media societies, and epidemic models with reasoning citizens. These simulations are valuable because they reproduce human-like macroscopic behaviour (business cycles, opinion polarisation, epidemic waves) without hand-coded behavioural rules. They are also expensive. single run of thousand-agent society can cost tens of dollars and tens of hours in API calls, which places systematic study, and in particular the study of how behaviour scales with the number of agents , out of reach for most researchers. The expense buys per-agent cognition, yet the scientific questions posed to these simulations are almost always macroscopic: does phase transition occur, what are the stylised facts of the aggregate, how does an observable scale with ? For such questions century of statistical physics offers lesson: the macroscopic behaviour of large interacting system is governed by few collective variables, and most microscopic detail is irrelevant to it. If that stance applies to LLM societies, 1 then for macroscopic purposes each expensive agent can be replaced by cheap surrogate whose few parameters are fitted from small number of queries, and the society can be studied at any on laptop. Whether the stance applies is not automatic, and the contribution of this paper is criterion for when it does. We argue that the deciding property is what each agent perceives. An agent that reacts to one population-wide aggregate (an inflation rate, global trending feed) sits in mean-field regime, and scalar surrogate reproduces the macroscopic observable with an error that vanishes as 1/2. An agent that reacts to signal shared only within its community, or only to its graph neighbours, sits in regime where the same scalar surrogate carries an error that does not vanish, and may even grow with . The taxonomy of Section 3 makes this precise by mapping the perception and memory design of simulation to cell, an effective theory, and predicted -trend of the surrogate error. Because the perception design of social simulation is in practice set by its recommender, the recommender is the switch between the regimes in which cheap modelling succeeds and those in which it fails. We validate the criterion in three ways. First, on faithful, code-authoritative reimplementation of the LLM macroeconomy EconAgent, we show that the surrogate reproduces the targets macroscopic signatures and that doing so exposes what those signatures do and do not measure. Second, we falsify the taxonomy directly: its cell assignments are pre-registered and then tested blind, both on held-out contact graphs and on the measured response function of real LLM. Third, we classify and reproduce eight named LLM simulations spanning all three perception cells: EconAgent, AgentTorch, OASIS, AgentSociety, De Marzo et al.s consensus game, Williams et al.s generative epidemic, LLMTravelers congestion game, and Generative Agents Smallville (with TwinMarkets financial stylised facts as documented boundary case), together with cross-domain check against differentiable agent-based model, using agent responses cloned throughout from genuine LLM decisions (DeepSeek by default; six models for the De Marzo cross-model test, and GPT-4o alongside DeepSeek for TwinMarket). Two findings of independent interest emerge. EconAgents frequently cited reproduction of Okuns law turns out to be an accounting identity that behaviour-free policy already satisfies, whereas its Phillips curve is genuine behavioural signature carried by single labour-cyclicality coefficient; we estimate that coefficient from cloned decisions and recover the macroscopic value as an out-of-sample prediction. And when the pipeline is driven by genuine LLM decisions, 2 2 ablation isolates the reasoning stepnot the wording of the promptas the cause of the emergent Phillips curve, so the cheap surrogate becomes an instrument: what makes the macro law appear is itself measurable.

sections.title: 2 Related work
sections.content: We connect several literatures that are rarely joined; fuller map of all 115 verified sources is given in the companion review [21]. Expensive LLM simulations such as Generative Agents [2], EconAgent [1], OASIS [4], and AgentSociety [5] establish that LLM societies reproduce human-like macroscopic phenomena and define the observables surrogate must hit, but none is paired with low-parameter model whose scaling is analysed. Sociophysics supplies the off-the-shelf few-parameter rules (voter and Ising models, boundedconfidence dynamics, kinetic opinion equations, and active-matter flocking dynamics [19]), leaving open which rule given LLM agent realises. Coarse-graining and equation learning, from mean-field 2 reductions to equation-free methods and archetype-based population models, compress dynamics but stop short of the finite-N closure problem and of LLM-specific targets. Mean-field game theory [16] and heterogeneous-agent macroeconomics [17] provide the limit and three cautions we adopt: one moment is often enough but misses the tails, small-N exponents can agree by accident, and shared driver can manufacture power law without phase transition. Finally, closure theory (the MoriZwanzig memory kernel [13], the BBGKY hierarchy [14], graphons [15], and inverse-Ising methods) supplies the machinery that our taxonomy invokes cell by cell. The closest prior work is MF-LLM [12], which couples population-level mean field to per-agent LLM decisions; it keeps the LLM in the loop and analyses no scaling, whereas we replace the agent and study the macroscopic observable as varies. The contribution of this paper is the join that no prior work makes: low-parameter surrogate per agent, fitted from genuine LLM decisions elicited on named LLM simulations own prompts to reproduce its macroscopic observable, together with classificatory layer that predicts the -trend of the surrogate error and is validated blind.

sections.title: 3 The perception-ordered taxonomy
sections.content: Let Φt denote the microscopic update of the LLM society and the projection onto the macroscopic observable of interest. cheap surrogate replaces Φt by low-parameter map ˆΦt acting on the projected variables. The surrogate reproduces the observable exactly when coarse-graining commutes with the dynamics, Φt = ˆΦtP ; in general it does not, and the size of the commutation defect Φt ˆΦtP is what the taxonomy predicts. We call the resulting gap in the macroscopic observable the surrogate error ; the commutation defect is the one-step, map-level quantity that drives it, and the two scale together (they coincide at the mean-field cell). In plain terms, the surrogate replaces every agent by single average agent, so it can be right only to the extent that the population is well summarised by its average, and what decides that is what each agent looks at. When every agent reacts to the same population-wide quantity (an inflation rate, global trending feed), the agents move together, the mean is sufficient statistic, and the only error is sampling noise that washes out as 1/ . When each agent instead reacts to private draw or to its own neighbourhood, the agents no longer share an input; averaging discards the structure that actually drives them, and the error stops falling with : it plateaus, or even grows. Perception thus decides whether averaging is legitimate at all, and memory whether the past must be tracked. We organise this defect along two coarse-graining axes: interaction order and memory. The first is the interaction order : how many other agents feed into single agents decision. global aggregate feed is order zero (every agent sees the same population statistic) and yields mean-field theory in which the scalar surrogate error is set by sampling noise and vanishes as 1/2. community feed, shared within each of fixed number of blocks, is heterogeneous mean field: the error no longer vanishes but falls only with the number of blocks, leaving an O(1) floor in . local feed, restricted to graph neighbours, is genuinely k-body, and the error is controlled by the degree structure rather than by . The second is memory: whether an agents decision depends only on current inputs or on an accumulated internal state. Long memory makes the dynamics non-Markovian and requires memory kernel in the closure. These two axes define the cells of Figure 1, and each cell names both predicted -trend of the surrogate error and the minimal closure that removes it: scalar mean field for the global cell, block or graphon mean field for the community cell, and pair approximation (a moment closure Figure 1: The perception cell sets the scaling of the surrogate error. simulations perception and memory design places it in one cell of the [interaction order memory] taxonomy. Each cell lists three things: its effective theory (top, bold), the predicted trend of the scalar-surrogate error with (middle), and the system(s) that validate that cell here (bottom, italic). The tint marks whether the cheap surrogate works (error falls with ), is conditional, or breaks (error stays O(1) or grows), as keyed at the right. that tracks two-agent correlations rather than only single-agent means [26]) with memory kernel for the local, long-memory cell. Two further axes refine the picture and are demanded by data presented later. shared driver that itself fluctuates makes the mean field random, so its fluctuations fall more slowly than the naive rate. And strongly curved per-agent response makes coarse-graining fail via Jensens inequality even under private feed, because the average of nonlinear response is not the response at the average. Collecting these, Φt ˆΦtP is bounded, heuristically, by sum of an interaction-order term, memory term, and response-curvature term. The first two are the classical BBGKY and MoriZwanzig contributions, and the third is the curvature axis that Section 5.6 isolates on real LLM. We treat this decomposition as an organising heuristic rather than theorem: the terms are not derived and the constant is not bounded.

sections.title: 4 Methods
sections.content: The method is one procedure, applied unchanged to every target in Section 5 (Algorithm 1): classify the simulations perception cell, which predicts the -trend of the surrogate error before any fitting; 6 Algorithm 1 The poor-mans recipe: replace each LLM agent by low-parameter surrogate, then scale the society. Require: target LLM simulation with its perception and memory specification; macroscopic observable ; the published value at conditions Ensure: low-parameter surrogate reproducing at any size where the cell permits, and prediction (made from the cell, before any fitting) of how the surrogate error scales with 1: Classify the perception cell: (order, memory) classify cell(S) predicts the error trend before any fitting 2: Screen : if behaviour-free policy already reproduces it, reject it is then an accounting identity 3: Elicit decisions: query the LLM on Ss own prompts over small state grid cached; few dollars 4: Clone the surrogate: θ clone(D) 5: Read the floors: (floor, ) perception floors(θ) fit the 212 parameters by behavioural cloning error floor and knee from the fitted response 6: Sweep geometrically with Ntarget: simulate the surrogate society and measure (N ) 7: Validate: compare (N ) to at and test the error trend against the cells prediction pre-registered screen the observable; elicit few hundred to few thousand genuine LLM decisions on the targets own prompts; clone low-parameter surrogate; read off its error floor and knee from the fitted response; and run the surrogate society to large on laptop, validating the macroscopic observable and checking the error trend against the cells prediction. The remainder of this section states the problem formally and details each component; the parenthetical step numbers refer to Algorithm 1. Problem statement. We are given target LLM society with microscopic update Φt, macroscopic observable fixed by the projection of Section 3, its published value at conditions C, and target size . We seek low-parameter surrogate map ˆΦt with parameter vector θ Rd, small, whose per-agent policy ˆπθ is fitted from real LLM decisions, such that coarse-graining commutes with the surrogate dynamics: the objective is to minimise the finite-size surrogate error ε(N ) = Φt ˆΦtP read out through the observable. Crucially, the parameters are fitted by (s,a) ℓ(cid:0)a, ˆπθ(s)(cid:1) over transfer set of behavioural cloning of the per-agent policy, θ = arg minθ teacher decisions (s, a), not by matching ; the macroscopic observable is therefore never fitted and is always an out-of-sample test, and the taxonomy of Section 3 predicts the trend of ε(N ) from the designs cell alone. (cid:80) The primary target that instantiates this problem is EconAgent [1] (step 6s environment), macroeconomy in which each household is GPT agent that decides monthly whether to work and how much to consume; the released code reproduces business-cycle signatures including Phillips and an Okun relation. We reimplement its market mechanics in NumPy so that surrogate can be dropped into an identical environment, and the reimplementation is code-authoritative: it chains the four published components (labour, progressive taxation, consumption, and savings) and reproduces the sign and magnitude of the released non-LLM baseline. Before an observable is used as validation target it must pass an a-priori screen (step 2), because not every macroscopic relation measures behaviour: we ask whether behaviour-free policy already produces it, and if so the observable is an accounting identity that validates nothing. This 7 discriminator is fixed in advance and applied uniformly. The behavioural content that survives is captured by cloning (steps 34). surrogate agent is twelve-parameter student: two logistic heads, one for the work decision and one for the consumption propensity, each linear in six features (a bias, three standardised state variables, the interest rate, and the macroscopic signal g), fitted from transfer set of (state, action) decisions produced by teacher. The teacher may be hand-specified policy or real LLM, and single loader makes the two kinds of trace interchangeable, so the same pipeline serves the controls and the LLM experiments. For the LLM experiments the teacher is DeepSeek (deepseek-chat, queried through its Anthropic-compatible endpoint), prompted on EconAgents own monthly household prompts; decisions are cached to disk, so fitted result re-runs at no cost, every paid run carries hard budget guard, and the total DeepSeek spend across the whole study is few dollars. The classification and finite-size steps (1 and 5) are carried by small reusable module: classify cell maps perception and memory spec to cell, and perception floors returns the mean-field error floors of fitted response. We validate these primitives against systems whose scaling is known exactly (the Minority Game and network epidemic models) before trusting them on LLM targets.

sections.title: 5 Results
sections.content: The experiments answer three questions. RQ1 (prediction): does simulations perception cell predict the sign of the surrogate errors -trend (vanishing, plateauing, or growing) before any agent is cloned? RQ2 (reproduction): can twoto twelve-parameter surrogate, fitted from few dollars of genuine LLM decisions, reproduce the published macroscopic behaviour of named LLM simulations across all three cells: the number within noise where matching it does not require the targets own model, and the mechanism and functional form where it does? RQ3 (mechanism): for given macroscopic observable, is it behavioural at all, and which single microscopic ingredient carries it? RQ1 is tested by the blind, pre-registered graph and perception experiments (Sections 5.5 5.6) and by the finite-size trend in every cell; RQ2 by EconAgent (Section 5.1) and the remaining named targets (Appendix E); RQ3 by the a-priori observable test and the identifiability and De Marzo analyses (Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.7).

sections.title: 5.1 EconAgent in the mean-field cell
sections.content: EconAgents published targets are Phillips correlation of 0.619 and an Okun correlation of 0.918. The a-priori test separates them. In EconAgent real GDP is, by construction, an affine-invertible function of the number of working agents (an R2 = 0.996 fit), so Okuns law relates quantity to an affine image of itself; behaviour-free Bernoulli(0.5) work policy already yields an Okun correlation of 0.998. Reproducing Okun therefore validates nothing. The Phillips curve is different: wage inflation is driven by goods-market imbalance with no direct employment-to-wage channel, so negative unemploymentinflation relation is genuine behavioural signature. Its mechanism is single procyclical-labour coupling: work propensity rising with the price signal. Fitting the twelve-parameter student to procyclical teacher recovers that coupling, and the macroscopic Phillips correlation, which never enters the fit, emerges as an out-of-sample prediction at 0.569 0.138, within noise of both the teacher and the published target ( = 0.05). non-procyclical teacher cloned through the identical pipeline gives vanishing 8 Micro channel price-keyed labour (proc g) countercyclical consumption employment-feedback labour most-negative Phillips reachable 0.80 0.43 +0.40 (wrong sign) reaches 0.62? yes no (saturates) no Table 1: The reachable Phillips frontier of three micro-channels. Only price-keyed labour reaches the published 0.62; near the frontier the mechanism is nearly identified by the single macroscopic number. Phillips; the coupling, not the pipeline, produces the effect. This is the mean-field cell in action: as grows from 20 to 500 the cloned Phillips strengthens monotonically from 0.29 to 0.86 as averaging over more agents reinforces the weak signal.

sections.title: 5.2 Identifiability is a frontier, not a degeneracy
sections.content: One macroscopic number need not pin the microscopic mechanism. We map the reachable Phillips frontier of three candidate micro-channels  (Table 1)  . Only labour keyed to the price signal reaches the published value, and near that frontier the channel is nearly pinned, though the pinning requires the coupling to sit at the upper end of its estimated range. Degeneracy is local rather than global: it occurs only at an intermediate value of the Phillips correlation where labour and consumption channel coexist, and there single additional aggregate observable (the sign of consumption propensity against unemployment, or of employment against the price level) separates them. So one macroscopic number is more identifying than naive under-determination concern would suggest, and where it is not, one more number suffices.

sections.title: 5.3 The triple join on genuine LLM decisions
sections.content: We now drive the pipeline with real LLM decisions: fit the student from budget of DeepSeek decisions elicited on EconAgents household prompts, drop it into the market, and recover the macroscopic observable. The runs cost $0.44 and $0.67 for three and six thousand decisions. The headline is that asking the model to reason is what produces the Phillips curve, and 2 2 ablation isolates it. EconAgents protocol gives GPT reasoning channel through quarterly reflection; the ablation below is our own elicitation probe. naive reasoning prompt confounds three changes (a chain-of-thought step, an amplified inflation wording, and an intensity adjective), so we cross whether the model reasons with whether the inflation signal is amplified, holding the numeric input to the student byte-identical across all four cells  (Table 2)  . The two factors are orthogonal: reasoning turns the chain-of-thought step on or off, while wording presents the same inflation figure in plain or in amplified language. Reading the four cells, with no reasoning the cloned Phillips is weak and even flips sign with wording (0.43 plain, +0.04 amplified), whereas with reasoning it is strongly negative under both wordings (0.73 and 0.66): turning reasoning on (moving down column) shifts the correlation sharply, and once reasoning is on the wording barely moves it (0.73 vs 0.66); wording matters only when reasoning is off, where it flips the sign. The reasoning effect is large and clearly resolved even where it is smallest: at plain wording, turning reasoning on shifts the correlation by 0.30 at difference standard error near 0.04 (the main effect across both wordings is 0.50), whereas the two reasoning cells are only marginally separated, so we do not claim one is robustly more negative than the other. 9 clone Phillips at = 100 (chat, 24 seeds) plain wording 0.43 0.18 no reasoning 0.73 0.10 reasoning (CoT) amplified wording +0.04 0.21 0.66 0. Table 2: Reasoning, not wording, drives the emergent Phillips curve. 2 2 ablation; the numeric signal fed to the student is identical across the four cells. The reproduction is modeland reasoning-conditional rather than robust. Under reasoning prompt DeepSeek-chats cloned Phillips is 0.665 0.12, the nearest cell landing 0.05 from the published 0.619; but sibling models under the same prompt scatter to 0.78 and 0.84, and no configuration reproduces the published value robustly. The exact value is model-andprompt fingerprint. The cheap surrogate is thus both cost-saving device and an instrument: what makes the macroscopic law shift (here, whether the agent reasons) is itself measurement. The clone also independently reproduces the mean-field scaling of Section 5.1, its terse-prompt Phillips strengthening from 0.34 at = 20 to 0.61 at = 500, so all three legs of the join close on genuine LLM data.

sections.title: 5.4 Closure-machinery checks on known ground truth
sections.content: Before trusting the taxonomy on LLM targets we certify its closure machinery on systems whose scaling is known exactly. On epidemic dynamics over contact graphs, scalar mean field is accurate on complete graph, degrades on k-regular graph, and fails near threshold on scale-free graph [20] and on real Facebook network, exactly as the interaction-order axis predicts. On the Minority Game [18], finite-size-scaling data collapse recovers the critical control parameter to within 13%; we therefore treat roughly 15% as the toolkits resolution floor and do not read precision below it. These controls are epidemics and games, not LLM agents; their role is to validate the machinery, not the LLM claims.

sections.title: 5.5 A blind test of the taxonomy on held-out graphs
sections.content: To make this test rather than fit, we pre-registered each cells assignment and its predicted -trend, then evaluated them on contact graphs held out from all calibration. All three predictions held. The mean-field cells error shrank with , the community cells settled to an O(1) floor, and the local cells tracked the degree structure; at large the three errors ordered themselves exactly as the assignment demanded. This validates the interaction-order axis on graph dynamics. The same axis, on real LLMs response function, is tested next (Section 5.6).

sections.title: 5.6 A blind test on the LLM perception layer
sections.content: The sharpest test of the perception axis is on real LLMs response function rather than on synthetic one. We fit the student to genuine DeepSeek reasoning trace and then feed population three signals with the same mean and, for the private and community cases, the same misperception variance, differing only in correlation structure: global feed that every agent shares, private feed drawn independently per agent, and community feed shared within each of fixed number of 10 Figure 2: The perception switch on real DeepSeek response function. Private misperception averages away; correlated community misperception leaves an O(1) floor that falls as B1/2; strongly curved response leaves Jensen floor even under private feed. blocks. The prediction, pre-registered, is that private noise averages away while community noise leaves floor that falls only with the number of blocks. On the near-linear consumption head all five pre-registered predictions held: the global and private errors fall as 1/2, the community error is flat in at an O(1) floor, that floor falls as B1/2 in the number of communities, and block-aware surrogate repairs it. The strongly saturating work head refutes two of its five predictions, and we report the refutation as measured: its private-feed error does not shrink but sits at floor of 0.018. post-hoc analysis, not pre-registered, identifies the cause as response curvature: the infinitepopulation Jensen bias Eεf (g + ε) (g) equals 0.018, matching the floor. The same curvature constant then predicts, with no further fitting, why the community floors B1/2 decay is broken on this head: the block-averaged floor cannot fall below the Jensen level, so its ratio across = 5 to 80 is compressed to about 2.0 against the ideal 4.0 and the measured 1.93, while the odd stance response of Appendix E.1 has zero Jensen bias by symmetry and obeys the clean law. The curvature term of the commutation heuristic thus turns from post-hoc diagnosis into confirmed quantitative prediction (Figure 2). It also confirms Proposition 2: the work heads fitted response gives knee = v1/m2 1 29, so its private-feed error should already be flat at the floor by = 100, as observed across = 100 to 3200; the consumption head gives 2.5 104, so it keeps improving throughout, as observed. Both mechanisms live on single axis. Holding the total misperception variance fixed and letting knob λ set the fraction that is community-shared rather than private sweeps real DeepSeek society across the mean-field boundary (Figure 3): the near-linear head sweeps cleanly from vanishing error at λ = 0 to an O(1) floor at λ = 1, the saturating head floors at the Jensen level for all λ, and the block-aware surrogate leaves residual equal to the Jensen floor scaled by the private fraction. Because the variance is fixed, this isolates correlation as the driver. To separate what the taxonomy fixes from what the individual model fixes, we refit fLLM on 11 Figure 3: The recommender dial. One knob λ (the community-shared fraction of the feed, at fixed misperception variance) moves the society across the predictability boundary; the two mechanisms (correlation break and curvature floor) separate on the one axis. thirteen elicitation traces spanning five independent labs (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta) and both plain and reasoning prompts, and re-ran the whole perception test on each (run xmodel perception.py, pre-registered before the traces were collected). The three predictions that define coarse-grainingthe global feed averages out, the correlated community feed leaves an O(1) floor, and block-aware closure repairs itheld for twelve of the thirteen. The single exception is gpt-4o-mini, the smallest model in the panel: its block-aware closure moves in the predicted direction, with the block error falling monotonically relative to the scalar error, but does not reach the factor-of-two criterion by = 3200. Every other model, including the three OpenAI flagships gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, and gpt-5.1, clears the core, so the failure tracks model capability rather than any one labs style. The one prediction that flips across models is that private feed also averages out, and it flips with each models response curvature: the Jensen bias runs from 104 (private error falls about fivefold with ) to 0.018 (private error flat in ), and the knee moves from 105 down to 140 in step, as Proposition 2 predicts.1 The cell assignment is therefore property shared across architectures rather than house style of one model family; the response curvature that sets the knee is property of the individual model, and the two vary independently.

sections.title: 5.7 De Marzo et al.: the critical group size is a perception limit
sections.content: De Marzo, Castellano and Garcıa [6] give published universal result: an LLM shown its peers opinions adopts the majority with probability (m) = 1 2 [tanh(βm) + 1], governed by one majorityforce β, with consensus (a macroscopic state in which the population aligns on one opinion) requiring β > 1 and critical group size Nc where β(N ) = 1. They report Nc growing with model capability: Nc 50 for Llama-3-70B, and only lower bounds ( 1000) for their more capable models, which they 1These cross-model knees are read empirically from the private-feed scan; for the primary DeepSeek trace this 1 of Section 5.6 gives 29 for the same trace. The two agree to an order of gives 140, whereas the analytic v1/m2 magnitude, the gap reflecting the folded-normal approximation in the empirical estimator. 12 could not push to consensus failure within the tested range. Across models Nc correlates strongly with the MMLU capability benchmark (r 0.75). This target lets us do more than reproduce mechanism: we can ask why finite critical group size exists at all, and the answer turns out to be the papers own variableperception. We fit β(N ) by maximum likelihood from real decisions elicited with their verbatim prompt across six models (Figure 4, Table 3). The measurement reproduces their universal form, and it exposes the mechanism. finite Nc cannot come from the mean-field response: the self-consistency = tanh(βm) has nonzero (consensus) solution for every when β > 1, and finite-N fluctuations only round the transition. Formally (the proof is in Appendix D): Proposition 4 (Consensus threshold and its crossing). The iterated response (cid:55) tanh(βm) is odd with Jacobian β at = 0. Its disordered fixed point = 0 is therefore stable iff β < 1 and loses stability at βc = 1 through supercritical pitchfork [25] (oddness excludes quadratic term), with ordered branch (cid:112)3(β 1) as β 1. Hence consensus exists iff β > 1, independently of . Consequence 5 (Finite Nc is perception threshold). finite critical group size therefore exists if and only if the measured slope βeff (N ) decays through 1. The slope βeff (N ) is the resolution with which an agent reads weak majority in list of opinions, so Nc is perception threshold, not thermodynamic one. The data confirm both halves. strong majority (m = 0.5) is read perfectly (P = 1) at every ; only the resolution of weak majority degrades with , and βeff (N ) is that resolution. Models split cleanly by whether their resolution decays  (Table 3)  : the reasoning models Opus-4.8 and GLM-5.2 count perfectly (βeff pegged, Nc = ), DeepSeek holds flat βeff 1.9 > 1 (Nc = , our pre-registered lower bound), while GPT-4o, Llama and GPT-4-Turbo show decaying βeff and hence finite Nc. The level is red herring: GPT-4os βeff 7 far exceeds DeepSeeks 1.9 yet GPT-4o loses consensus first, because only the asymptote relative to 1 matters. This aligns with the Weber/approximate-number-system law [9]: numerosity discrimination depends on the ratio nk/nz = (1 + m)/(1 m), which is -independent at fixed majority fraction, so perfect ratio-perceiver would have flat βeff and Nc = ; finite Nc is deviation from that ideal (attention mass 1/N diluted over long list). The literature supports the substrate (LLM magnitude representations are log-compressive, Weber-like [9]), though it cautions that this representational geometry does not by itself guarantee ideal behavioural ratio-perception, so we lean on it as motivation rather than proof. De Marzo et al. themselves attribute the β-decline to an information-processing limit, and report Nc correlating with MMLU (r 0.75)capability, not thermodynamics. We probe the mechanism interventionally. Handing GPT-4o the explicit tally (nk, nz) in the prompt (removing the list-reading load while leaving the social decision unchanged) flattens its βeff (N ) from decay to pegged constant, sending Nc ; DeepSeek, already flat, is unchanged. The decay that generates finite Nc is therefore the list-to-count perception step, not the opinion dynamics. (The intervention also lengthens the prompt by one sentence, length/salience change we did not separately control; pure-perception control that asks only which opinion is more common (no adoption) corroborates, giving GPT-4o flat β in , so the effect is not generic prompt-length artefact.) consequence for this papers own agenda: Nc is not finite-size-scaling critical point; it is bifurcation in an externally driven perception control parameter, with no diverging correlation length, so data-collapse in is the wrong lens here; one should measure βeff (N ) and locate its crossing of 1. model Opus-4.8 GLM-5.2 DeepSeek-chat GPT-4-Turbo GPT-4o Llama-3.3-70B βeff (N ) trend pegged (perfect count) pegged flat 1.9 slow decay decay decay our Nc 1600 900 1600 50 (Llama-3) De Marzo 1000 (l.b.) unreported Table 3: The critical group size is set by whether perception resolution decays. Models whose βeff (N ) stays above 1 have Nc = ; those whose resolution decays through 1 have finite Nc, recovered from the finite-N naming-game dynamics on the fitted response. The load-bearing result is the finite/infinite split, which is consistent with De Marzo et al. wherever the models overlap: the one model they pin as finite (Llama-3) we also find finite, and the models we find flat post-date their study. Absolute values we do not claim to match: our static probe over-estimates βeff at small , we used Llama-3.3 rather than their Llama-3, and De Marzo et al. pin only Llama-3-70B ( 50) with the rest lower bounds, so the fine ordering is not established either way. GPT-4-Turbos 1600 is at least consistent with their 1000 lower bound.

sections.title: 5.8 A measured memory kernel
sections.content: Appendix E.1s honest weakness is that only the assimilation rate is fitted while the memory that drives polarisation is posited. We measure it. Eliciting DeepSeek attitude updates given controlled history of past interactions, we recover discrete MoriZwanzig kernel by regression, anext (cid:80) τ K(τ ) (ptτ a) (Figure 5). All three pre-registered predictions held. The currentinteraction weight K(0) = 0.27 is in the range of the independently fitted µ = 0.415 and, tellingly, below it, since an existing history damps the current move: the conviction-braking signature seen directly. The past-interaction tail is real, at 47% of K(0), so the update is genuinely non-Markovian. And the tail is concentrated in the first few lags and vanishes beyond, so finite memory closure captures it. The memory axis is thus grounded empirically in the LLM layer, alongside the perception axis.

sections.title: 6 Discussion
sections.content: The results support single organising claim. Whether low-parameter surrogate can reproduce the macroscopic observable of an LLM society is decided by the societys perception and memory design, and the deciding structure can be read off before the simulation is run. global aggregate feed places the society in mean-field cell where scalar surrogate reproduces the observable with an error that vanishes as 1/2; community or graph-structured feed places it in cells where the error is O(1) or grows, and where the surrogate must resolve the responsible structure through block, graphon, or pair-plus-memory closure. Two axes beyond interaction order and memory matter in practice: shared driver that itself fluctuates, and curved peragent response that breaks coarse-graining through Jensens inequality even under private feed. Empirically the operative control turned out to be the recommender: because it sets simulations perception design, it is what moves society across the boundary between the regimes where cheap modelling succeeds and where it fails (Appendix E.1 and Section 5.6). 14 Figure 4: De Marzo consensus is perception crossing. The published adoption form transfers to new model (left); the majority force βeff (N ) is the perception resolution, and finite critical group size exists only where it decays through the threshold βc = 1 (right). The cheap surrogate is not only cost-saving device but an instrument. Because its few parameters are estimated rather than tuned, the value that reproduces macroscopic law becomes measurement of what produces that law: single labour-cyclicality coefficient for EconAgents Phillips curve, reasoning step rather than phrasing for its magnitude, saturating societal response for Williams epidemic, decaying memory kernel for AgentSocietys polarisation, and perception resolution βeff (N ) whose crossing of 1 sets De Marzos critical group size. Turning the surrogates fit and its failures into measurements is, in our view, the more durable contribution.

sections.title: 7 Limitations
sections.content: Several limitations bound the claims. The named-target reproductions are mechanism-and-scaling matches, and the two that go further reproduce targets published functional form on new model rather than its own models published number; the strongest test (running targets exact models to hit its published macroscopic number) remains open. The EconAgent market is code-calibrated reimplementation validated against the released non-LLM baseline, and the DeepSeek decisions drive the agents rather than the market mechanics. The commutation decomposition is an organising heuristic, not theorem. The pre-registrations bind specific numeric predictions with named kill criteria, but each was committed to our own repository together with its result, so the git history does not by itself separate prediction from data. We document this candidly and archive the pre-registration bundle, with per-file SHA-256 hashes, at an external timestamped DOI [22]; this anchors the content immutably to third party, though it dates the deposit, not the prediction. Finally, the LLM-layer results rest on one primary model, and where sibling models were tested the macroscopic value moved, which is itself part of the finding rather than nuisance. 15 Figure 5: measured memory kernel. The current assimilation sits below the memoryless rate (conviction braking); the past-interaction tail is real, decaying, and truncatable.

sections.title: 8 Conclusion
sections.content: We have argued that large LLM societies can, for macroscopic purposes, be modelled without large compute budget, and that whether this works is decided by perception-ordered taxonomy that maps simulations design to an effective theory and predicted trend of the surrogate error with . We tested the taxonomy against blind, pre-registered predictions on both of its axes at the LLM layer, traced its two refuted predictions quantitatively to response curvature, showed the classification to be automatable, quantified the elicitation and capacity cost of the macroscopic law through distillation scaling law, and reproduced eight named LLM simulations and differentiable agent-based model on genuine, cheaply elicited decisions. The recurring lesson is that the surrogates fit is measurement: the microscopic property that macroscopic observable depends on is exposed, not hidden, by replacing the expensive agent with cheap one.

sections.title: Reproducibility
sections.content: Every result has runner and cached decision trace, so seeded results reproduce deterministically and the LLM experiments re-run at no cost; the perception and scaling primitives, the preregistrations with their outcomes, and the figure scripts are included. Total elicitation across the study is few dollars of DeepSeek.

sections.title: E External validation suite
sections.content: The main text carries the load-bearing experiments: EconAgent, the two blind tests, De Marzo, and the measured memory kernel. This appendix collects the remaining validations and supporting checks: further named LLM simulations spanning the other perception cells, cross-domain comparison against automatic differentiation, distillation scaling law, an automated cell classifier, and two negative results. Each is self-contained confirmation of the taxonomy, not separate study. E.1 Named targets across the perception cells We now classify and reproduce named LLM simulations, each on genuine LLM decisions (DeepSeek unless noted), using the recipe: low-parameter response, the minimal closure named by its cell, and the cells predicted -trend. None matches targets exact same-model published number, which would require running that targets own models; Section 5.7 and Appendix E.5 come closest by reproducing targets published functional form on new model. AgentTorch: behaviour global, contagion local. AgentTorch [3] is million-agent LLM epidemic model (its case study is COVID-19 in New York City); it reaches that scale by querying the LLM once per demographic archetype and broadcasting the answer. We confirm from real DeepSeek archetype decisions why this works: the isolation behaviour is global feed, so the 20 Figure 6: AgentTorch spans two cells. Behaviour is global feed where the archetype trick is valid; contagion is local, where well-mixed surrogate over-predicts the peak and clustering, not the degree tail, drives the break. archetype error shrinks with the number of archetypes, whereas contagion runs on contact graph, where well-mixed surrogate over-predicts the peak and the break is driven by clustering rather than by the degree tail (Figure 6). OASIS: the recommender is the switch. OASIS [4] is social-media simulation of up to million agents, modelled on and Reddit; it ships two recommender modes, and the mode is the perception switch. Its Reddit hot-score feed is single global leaderboard: the cloned herd experiment converges to its mean-field value with an error that effectively vanishes. Its interest feed is per-community echo chamber: the group-polarisation error is O(1) and falls as B1/2 in the number of communities, and block-aware surrogate repairs it (Figure 7). The stance response fitted from 800 real DeepSeek decisions weights the agents own prior (α = 1.17) above the feed (κ = 0.60), yet the community feed still breaks the mean field. This response is odd about the operating point, so its Jensen bias vanishes (Consequence 1) and the break here is pure interaction-order effect, not curvature. AgentSociety: the hardest cell. AgentSociety [5] simulates over ten thousand agents in data-grounded urban society, and sits in the local, long-memory cell. scalar mean field cannot represent its between-block polarisation at all (the first-moment closure returns zero, so its error is the polarisation itself), and the error grows with under densifying interaction schedule while remaining bounded O(1) floor at fixed degree. pair-plus-memory closure repairs it, and an ablation of the conviction memory collapses most of the polarisation, isolating the memory axis (Figure 8). Only the assimilation rate (µ = 0.415) is fitted from data here; Section 5.8 measures the memory dependence that the rest of the mechanism posits. E.2 cross-domain check: closure versus autodiff The recipe is not specific to LLM agents. GradABM [11] makes million-agent epidemic differentiable and calibrates it by gradient descent on GPUs. For the aggregate mortality curve this is more Figure 7: OASIS: the two recommender modes are the perception switch. Global hot-score feed mean field; per-community interest feed an O(1) floor falling as B1/2. machinery than the science needs. On self-generated network epidemic we lift heterogeneous mean field from susceptible-infected to the full compartmental model, thirteen degree blocks coupled through degree-weighted infectious fraction, and calibrate two parameters by derivative-free simplex. It recovers the transmission rate to within 13% and the fatality rate to within 6% at mortality-curve RMSE of 22, in 0.34 seconds on laptop, against well-mixed baseline that misfits at RMSE 48 (a factor of 2.2) and against roughly 400 seconds of GPU forward-time per county for the differentiable model (Figure 9). We recover the method and the planted parameters, not the authors number on their data. E.3 distillation scaling law How much LLM does the macro law cost? Offline from the cached EconAgent trace we measure the Phillips error as joint function of the elicitation budget B, the surrogate capacity p, and the population (Figure 10). The error falls with budget, reaching tolerance by couple of thousand decisions; it falls with capacity and plateaus at four features; and the two axes are approximately separable, the error grid being ninety percent rank-one in log-error. The load-bearing feature is capacity floor: below four features the error plateaus above tolerance for any budget, so the surrogate is capacity-limited and buying more decisions cannot help, whereas above it the surrogate is data-limited and converges. The purchasing rule is therefore to buy structure first and data second: four features and one to two thousand decisions, well under dollar of DeepSeek. E.4 The classification is automatable The cell assignments above were made by hand. They need not be. Given only neutral description of simulations perception and memory design, with no taxonomy term leaked, an LLM emits the structured specification that classify cell consumes; the resulting cell matched the hand assignment in all eight cases we tested, including Generative Agents, correctly placed in the local, long-memory cell; the classifier saw no taxonomy term, though we wrote the neutral descriptions 22 Figure 8: AgentSociety in the local, long-memory cell. Scalar mean-field error grows under densification and floors at fixed degree; pair-plus-memory closure repairs it, and removing the conviction memory collapses the break. and cannot rule out that these published systems appear in its training data. The classificatory layer is pre-flight check for which surrogate will work, runnable before any expensive simulation. E.5 Williams et al.: generative epidemic in the mean-field cell Williams et al. [7] give generative agents daily stay-home decision from their symptoms and town-wide broadcast of new-infection prevalence. They publish three signatures: stay-home logistic regression (positive on symptoms, positive on prevalence, negative on prevalence squared, i.e. saturating response); flattened epidemic curve; and shift from single wave to several as the reproduction number falls. From 462 real DeepSeek decisions on their verbatim prompt we reproduce all three levels (Figure 11). The fitted logistic has the published sign structure, including the negative squared term (1.77, stronger saturation than their 0.65), tying the epidemics societal channel to the same response curvature that Section 5.6 isolated. Dropping the fitted response into behaviour-coupled compartmental model flattens the peak to seventh of the no-feedback baseline and roughly doubles the duration, with single wave at high reproduction number and multiple waves at low. And the cell is mean field: the scalar surrogates error against finite-N stochastic model shrinks with . E.6 LLMTraveler: filling the empty cell Every target so far has short memory except AgentSociety, which is k-local. The [mean-field long-memory] cell (a global signal with an accumulated history) was empty. LLMTraveler [8] fills it: LLM commuters play day-to-day congestion game, each day seeing the exponentially weighted moving average of their travel time on each route (the memory) and choosing route, with congestion felt only through the aggregate flow. The published result is that mean travel times converge to the Dynamic User Equilibrium (DUE), most models landing within 10% (GPT-4o +1.33%). We elicit real DeepSeek route 23 Figure 9: Closure versus autodiff. gradient-free degree-aware closure recovers the mortality curve and the planted parameters roughly 103 times faster than the differentiable million-agent model, for the aggregate observable. choices and fit two-parameter rule (switch) = σ(β γ) in the travel-time gap (prereg prereg llmtraveler 2026-07-03.md, Figure 12). The rule is rational (β = +0.40, it prefers the faster route) though it shows little of the inertia the authors report (γ 0 on DeepSeek, model-dependent difference). Run as day-to-day dynamic on the 16-traveler two-route network, it converges to the DUE at +4.7%, inside the published 10% band, with persistent switching around equilibrium as the authors also observe. The cell is confirmed too: the equilibrium gap mean DUE shrinks with the number of travelers (a mean-field flow convergence), so the surrogate reproduces the Wardrop user equilibrium [27] (the flow at which no traveler can reduce their own travel time by switching route unilaterally, here the same fixed point as the DUE above) at any on laptop. E.7 TwinMarket: the stylised facts need the market, not just the agent Not every target yields to compact surrogate, and the failure is informative. TwinMarket [10] reports that GPT-4o BDI investors reproduce the canonical stylised facts of financial returns (fat tails and volatility clustering) from rich beliefdesireintention state with social feed. We elicit real trading decisions (DeepSeek and GPT-4o) on compact state (recent trend, peer signal, own P&L) and fit low-parameter trader (prereg prereg twinmarket 2026-07-03.md). The trader recovers the behavioural signs (trend-following, herding on the peer signal, disposition effect, selling into profit) on both models. Yet dropped into minimal price-impact market at moderate coupling the trader does not generate fat tails: the returns stay near-Gaussian (excess kurtosis 0), because the elicited herding leaves the market subcritical. The boundary here is not the traders capacity but an un-elicited ingredient: the strength of the price-impact coupling. Raising that coupling makes the same weak trader supercritical (excess kurtosis rises past 7), so the stylised facts are under-determined by the elicited response alone: reproducing them needs the market mechanism, not just the agent, and our 24 Figure 10: distillation scaling law. The macro-observable error against elicitation budget and surrogate capacity p; capacity floor no budget can cross, and an approximately separable grid. compact surrogate does not fit that mechanism from LLM decisions. We report this honestly as the limit of eliciting only the agent, distinct from the data/capacity floor of Appendix E.3. E.8 Smallville: the fields most-cited numbers Generative Agents [2] produced the most-cited macro numbers in the area: in Smallvilles 25 agents, an invitation to Valentines party spreads by word-of-mouth to 13 of 25, and 5 attend. This is the [k-local long-memory] cell: local acquaintance cascade with agents remembering they were told.
